title.narrative: Enhancing Wastewater, Nutrient Management and Sanitation Provision for Marginalized Coastal Communities in Sabah, Malaysia

description.narrative:
The project will focus on the local, marginalized communities of Sabah, especially at the village of Lok Urai and potentially to include Mabul Island, directly affected by marine pollution, especially wastewater and nutrients. Through this new project, UNEP, UN-Habitat, and local implementing partners such as ACT Malaysia aim to provide solutions to address the degradation of the marine ecosystems, lay the foundations for a financial facility for scaling up similar interventions at local level, and finally, generate stronger government support to tackle this problem at national level.
Through Output 1, the community will benefit from solutions to tackle water pollution, and it is expected that at least 500 people, including women and girls (approximately 200), will benefit from the intervention. Output 2 is fully focused on capacity-building and knowledge exchange for relevant stakeholders and representatives of wastewater utilities. It is expected that at least 200 people will benefit from this output. The same group will be the target of Outputs 3 and 4. Output 3 will additionally focus on developing guidelines to create a community cooperative that helps scale up action, finance, and business opportunities in the field of sanitation provision, as well as wastewater and nutrient management. Output 4 will focus on communication and visibility of the project, as well as evaluation. The previous interventions in Sabah have been successful also thanks to the good visibility received thanks to web stories, exposure to the SDG 6 Best Practices competition, and internal UNEP innovation award contest. For this project, the team plans to produce a web story, an interactive story map with interviews from the targeted group and stakeholders, a factsheet and any other outreach product that can help disseminate the results achieved by the project team. The products developed under Output 4 will be crucial to secure more funding towards scaling up this intervention in other areas of Sabah, Malaysia and possibly even beyond within the region.
However, further local, and marginalized communities of Sabah, for example at Mabul Island, will ultimately benefit from investments by the government and other donors stemming from this project and scaling up of similar interventions. The project will address these issues by delivering against four outputs and eleven activities all aimed at addressing the issues of sanitation provision, nutrient, and wastewater management in Lok Urai, and at the city level in Kota Kinabalu. Despite having a focus on these areas, lessons learned from the activities in Lok Urai possess the potential to be replicated elsewhere. Meanwhile, the project aims to leverage additional funding and create opportunities for addressing wastewater pollution across Sabah, especially as this pertains to domestic wastewater.
Another potential area that the project will include in terms of engagement with the authorities is the island of Mabul, located in the north-eastern side of Sabah. Mabul is one of the best diving resorts of Sabah, but at the same time, it is affected by similar problems as Lok Urai and the City of Kota Kinabalu when it comes to wastewater and nutrient pollution. It has been reported that water pollution is affecting tourism, and a solution to address this issue in Mabul is also urgently needed.
The project results are meant to generate policies that will be helpful for Sabah and Malaysia to drive change around wastewater, nutrient management, and sanitation provision. In addition, the project is structured and will be implemented in a way that looks at scaling up and replication as a priority. This will be ensured through extensive coordination and consultation with the partners, and relevant stakeholders. For instance, training will be delivered with those households where in-situ improvements of wastewater are applicable in the pilot area/city, to ensure their continued upkeep and maintenance of assets, and appreciation for clean water and sanitation.
During the implementation phase, the lead organization and partners will seek and tap into any other existing opportunity to seek additional financial support and involvement of key stakeholders for the next phase of this intervention. In addition, the results of the project will be reported back to the UNEP Committee of Permanent Representatives (CPR) and UN-Habitat Cities Investment Facility (CIF), through the periodic reporting exercise which will ensure visibility to the project and possible opportunities for seeking further financial support.
